_what: Discrepancies between supabase/migrations/*.sql and the applied-migration ledger that already existed when tool/migration_ledger_check.py was written (2026-08-17). Accepted, not hidden: every run prints them, and an entry here that has since been REPAIRED fails the check, so this file can only shrink.
_why_not_repaired: Repairing means rewriting 101 rows of production bookkeeping. The 10 misstamped rows could be repointed safely and probably should be; the 70 unapplied files cannot be fixed by repointing at all, since they have no row to repoint. Both are Jean's call, not a side effect of adding a checker. Note the practical consequence while they stand: `supabase db push` would consider all 80 of those files pending and try to run them again. That path is already unusable here (no SUPABASE_DB_PASSWORD), but it is the reason to fix this rather than live with it.
_measured: 2026-08-17, against yftazblpmicqtamyiwyb: 251 files, 198 ledger rows, 101 discrepancies — 70 unapplied, 19 unmirrored, 10 misstamped, 2 ambiguous. On 2026-08-17 the first real cold replay proved these are not merely untidy: seat_reassignment_log and three seat functions existed in production with no file at all, and five migrations could not replay without them. Repaired by 20260510182000, which is recorded here as applied the way `supabase migration repair --status applied` does — every object it creates is already present on production, and re-running it would rewrite live function source for no functional gain.
